title: Kernel of a two-term complex with free degree-0 term commutes with base change when Tor_1 and Tor_2 of the cokernel vanish
statement: Let $B$ be a commutative ring, $C$ a $B$-module, and $\delta:N_1\to N_0$ a homomorphism of $B$-modules with $N_0$ a free $B$-module; put $H_1=\ker\delta$ and $H_0=\operatorname{coker}\delta$. If $\operatorname{Tor}^B_1(H_0,C)=0$ and $\operatorname{Tor}^B_2(H_0,C)=0$ [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], then the $B$-linear map $H_1\otimes_BC\to\ker(\delta\otimes\mathrm{id}_C:N_1\otimes_BC\to N_0\otimes_BC)$, $h\otimes c\mapsto h\otimes c$ (induced by the inclusion $H_1\subseteq N_1$; it lands in the kernel since $\delta(h)=0$), is an isomorphism. (If $C$ is a $B$-algebra, this map is $C$-linear.)

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00S2 (lemma-exact-sequence-NL), final paragraph, lines 35462--35484

proof.text: Put $I=\operatorname{im}\delta\subseteq N_0$, let $j:I\to N_0$ be the inclusion, $\delta':N_1\to I$ the corestriction of $\delta$ (so $\delta=j\circ\delta'$, $\delta'$ surjective), $\iota:H_1=\ker\delta\to N_1$ the inclusion and $p:N_0\to H_0=N_0/I$ the projection. Then $0\to H_1\xrightarrow{\iota}N_1\xrightarrow{\delta'}I\to0$ and $0\to I\xrightarrow{j}N_0\xrightarrow{p}H_0\to0$ are short exact sequences of $B$-modules: $\ker\delta'=\ker\delta$ since $j$ is injective, and $\operatorname{im}j=I=\ker p$ by definition of the cokernel.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00S2 (lemma-exact-sequence-NL), final paragraph, lines 35462--35484 (the source writes $M$ for $I$)

proof.text: $I\otimes_BC\xrightarrow{j\otimes1}N_0\otimes_BC$ is injective. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tor-long-exact-first-variable] to $0\to I\xrightarrow{j}N_0\xrightarrow{p}H_0\to0$ and $N=C$: the sequence $\operatorname{Tor}^B_1(N_0,C)\to\operatorname{Tor}^B_1(H_0,C)\xrightarrow{\delta_C}I\otimes_BC\xrightarrow{j\otimes1}N_0\otimes_BC\xrightarrow{p\otimes1}H_0\otimes_BC\to0$ is exact. Exactness at $I\otimes_BC$ gives $\ker(j\otimes1)=\operatorname{im}\delta_C$, which is $0$ because $\operatorname{Tor}^B_1(H_0,C)=0$ by hypothesis. (This is the exact sequence $0\to M\otimes_BC\to N^0\otimes_BC\to H^0\otimes_BC\to0$ of the source.)

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00S2 (lemma-exact-sequence-NL), final paragraph, lines 35462--35484, lines 35470--35475

proof.text: $\operatorname{Tor}^B_1(I,C)=0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tor-dimension-shift-free] with $R=B$, the short exact sequence $0\to I\xrightarrow{j}N_0\xrightarrow{p}H_0\to0$ (whose middle term $N_0$ is free by hypothesis), $N=C$ and $i=1$: $\operatorname{Tor}^B_1(I,C)\cong\operatorname{Tor}^B_2(H_0,C)$, and the right side is $0$ by hypothesis.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00S2 (lemma-exact-sequence-NL), final paragraph, lines 35462--35484, lines 35476--35478 ('Since $N^0$ is free, we also see that $\text{Tor}_2^B(H^0, C) = \text{Tor}_1^B(M, C)$')

proof.text: $\iota\otimes1:H_1\otimes_BC\to N_1\otimes_BC$ is injective with image $\ker(\delta'\otimes1)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tor-long-exact-first-variable] to $0\to H_1\xrightarrow{\iota}N_1\xrightarrow{\delta'}I\to0$ (step 1) and $N=C$: the sequence $\operatorname{Tor}^B_1(N_1,C)\to\operatorname{Tor}^B_1(I,C)\xrightarrow{\delta_C}H_1\otimes_BC\xrightarrow{\iota\otimes1}N_1\otimes_BC\xrightarrow{\delta'\otimes1}I\otimes_BC\to0$ is exact. Since $\operatorname{Tor}^B_1(I,C)=0$ (step 3), exactness at $H_1\otimes_BC$ gives $\ker(\iota\otimes1)=0$, and exactness at $N_1\otimes_BC$ gives $\operatorname{im}(\iota\otimes1)=\ker(\delta'\otimes1)$. (This is the exact sequence $0\to H^{-1}\otimes_BC\to N^{-1}\otimes_BC\to M\otimes_BC\to0$ of the source.)

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00S2 (lemma-exact-sequence-NL), final paragraph, lines 35462--35484, lines 35478--35482

proof.text: Conclusion. Since $\delta=j\circ\delta'$, functoriality of $-\otimes_BC$ gives $\delta\otimes\mathrm{id}_C=(j\otimes1)\circ(\delta'\otimes1)$, and as $j\otimes1$ is injective (step 2), $\ker(\delta\otimes\mathrm{id}_C)=\ker(\delta'\otimes1)$. The map of the statement is $\iota\otimes1$ with its target restricted to $\ker(\delta\otimes\mathrm{id}_C)$ (on generators $h\otimes c\mapsto\iota(h)\otimes c$); by step 4 it is injective and its image is $\ker(\delta'\otimes1)=\ker(\delta\otimes\mathrm{id}_C)$, so it is a bijective $B$-linear map, hence an isomorphism of $B$-modules. If $C$ is a $B$-algebra, $\iota\otimes1$ commutes with the $C$-module structures $c'\cdot(x\otimes c)=x\otimes c'c$ on both sides (checked on generators), so the map is $C$-linear.
